A Russian strike on the center of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown, Kryvyi Rih, killed two people and wounded 60 others, local officials said Saturday.
Meanwhile, a Russian cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad caught fire in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday after it was hit by drones, Finnish and Russian officials said. It was not clear who struck the ship not far from the Russian border. The Finnish prime minister warned that the war was spilling into the region.
Read moreDrone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland
A 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman were killed in the attack Friday night on Kryvyi Rih in central Ukraine, Oleksandr Vilkul, the head of the city administration, wrote on Telegram. Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the regional military administration, said 60 people were wounded, including six children.
The strike caused four fires and damaged about 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools and an industrial facility, as well as businesses and vehicles, Vilkul said.
Video footage published by the regional branch of the Ukrainian State Emergency Service appeared to show further strikes while ambulance and firefighting crews were responding at the scene, as fires burned around them.
“First, two ballistic missiles. And then, when the emergency and rescue operation began, three more rockets hit doctors, rescuers and utility workers,” Vilkul wrote on Telegram.
The attack added to uncertainty about the prospects for ongoing talks brokered by Washington. It also came hours after two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland, in what its prime minister said was likely a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country.
In the unprecedented two-week military exercise that began November 9 in southeastern Poland, forces are preparing for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine aimed at helping to stabilize the country and rebuild its military. European countries previously have expressed alarm at what they deem to be Russia’s attempts to destabilize the continent.
NATO will defend every inch of Polish territory, Rutte says
NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte, speaking to reporters in Warsaw on Saturday, called the airspace violation “dangerous” and said all allies stood “in full solidarity with Poland.”
“NATO will defend every inch of Polish territory,” Rutte said. He said the alliance functioned “as it should” on Friday morning, when NATO jets supported Polish F-16s scrambled as Russian objects approached Polish airspace. NATO’s top military commander was assessing the alliance’s defenses and would make adjustments if needed, Rutte said.
The head of NATO forces in Europe, General Alexus Grynkewich, would do everything necessary to identify any threats to defense and deterrence capabilities and would implement appropriate adjustments if needed, Rutte said.
On Monday, a meeting of NATO's North Atlantic Council will be held in Brussels to discuss the violation of Polish airspace by Russian missiles, PAP also reported on Saturday.
"In the near future, we will receive strong support from our NATO allies to bolster the protection of our eastern border," Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz wrote on X on Saturday, commenting on the meeting of the NATO body.
"I've been in contact today with general Grynkewich, to coordinate the details of these measures."
Zelensky reaffirms Ukraine's wish to join NATO
Zelensky on Saturday reiterated his country's determination to join NATO, following proposals to provide Kyiv with security guarantees similar to those of the military alliance.
"Of course Ukraine very much wants to be in NATO," Zelensky told reporters, judging that membership of the alliance was one of the "most obvious security guarantees" for his country.
The issue of Ukraine joining NATO, ruled out by Washington since 2025, resurfaced in recent days during fresh talks to end the war nearly five years after Russia's invasion.
At a meeting with Kyiv's allies in Berlin on Thursday, US envoy Jared Kushner said Washington could be ready to grant Ukraine a security guarantee similar to that provided under Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty.
That clause -- the cornerstone of NATO -- states that an attack on one member is considered an attack on all allies.
Putin 'doesn’t want to stop the war'
At a meeting with UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting in Kyiv, Zelensky said Saturday that Ukraine’s repeated attacks on the Kerch Bridge linking occupied Crimea with the Russian mainland were a “fair response” to scores of Russian attacks on Ukrainian bridges. He said that Russia President Vladimir Putin had "attacked Ukrainian bridges 109 times.”
“Not the number of missiles — the number of attacks,” he said. “This is important, that’s why it’s our absolutely fair response.”
The Ukrainian leader said Putin “doesn’t want to stop the war” and is looking to escalate. He also rejected Putin’s claim that the Kerch bridge is used exclusively by civilian traffic.
“If he can use internet, he can use it and see tanks, armored vehicles, artillery,” the Ukrainian leader said.

items.summary:
Noni Madueke salvages draw for Arsenal at Newcastle United as Raya injured
League leaders Arsenal miss the chance to go eight points clear of second placed Brighton, who play on Sunday.
Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-
items.text:
Noni Madueke salvages draw for Arsenal at Newcastle United as Raya injured
League leaders Arsenal miss the chance to go eight points clear of second placed Brighton, who play on Sunday.
Arsenal missed the chance to open up an eight-point lead at the top of the Premier League after a stirring second-half fightback from Newcastle held the defending champions to a 2-2 draw.
The Gunners led on Saturday through Eberechi Eze’s strike after a dominant first 45 minutes.
But Mikel Arteta’s men were suddenly headed for defeat when goals from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw provided a much-needed boost for under-fire Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle.
Noni Madueke salvaged a point for Arsenal and stretched their lead at the top over surprise package Brighton to six points.
However, the loss of influential goalkeeper David Raya to injury could provide a twist in the title race that many believed Arsenal would cruise.
Newcastle remain in the bottom half of the table with just one win in six games in all competitions.
Yet, Jaissle can point to his side’s second-half performance as a potential turning point after a difficult start to his reign at St James’ Park.
Arsenal move back six points clear of third-placed Manchester City, but missed the chance to put their foot down in the defence of their title.
Madueke continued his impressive form in the injury absence of Bukayo Saka and hit the post early on.
Former Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes was roundly booed on his first return to Tyneside since making a 75 million pound ($98m) move to the Emirates Stadium in August.
The Brazilian nearly silenced his former faithful when he prodded just wide from a Madueke cross as Arsenal pressed for the opener.
It duly arrived 10 minutes before the break when Kai Havertz pounced on a poor touch by Lewis Hall and brilliantly played in Eze to blast high past Lukas Hornicek.
Jaissle got the response he needed from his half-time team talk as Newcastle came out a completely different proposition after the break.
Arsenal also played a part in letting the home side back into the game and lifting the 50,000 crowd in doing so.
Martin Odegaard shanked his attempt at a long ball forward to allow William Osula to play in Barnes to level.
Suddenly, an Arsenal side that had kept seven clean sheets in their opening 10 league games was on the rocks.
Thiaw bundled home a second for Newcastle just 13 minutes later after Dan Burn was left completely unmarked from a corner and his header was only parried by Raya.
That proved to be one of Raya’s final interventions as the Spaniard had to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.
Raya would be a massive miss if the Spaniard is sidelined for a significant spell.
But Arsenal regained their composure in time to salvage a point that keeps them well in the driving seat to retain the title.
Odegaard made amends for his earlier error by freeing Madueke down the righ,t and he cut inside before his tame deflected shot found a way past Hornicek.
Madueke told Sky Sports that he thought 2-2 was a “fair” result.
“Game of two halves is fair. First half we were outstanding. Should have got three goals, to be honest. Missed a couple of chances myself. Everything else was there,” he said.
“The second half, the first 20 minutes, was not good by our standard. When you give this team and crowd belief at home, it is difficult. We showed character to get back in the game, but 2-2 is a fair result.”

items.title: Noni Madueke rescues point for Arsenal in seesaw draw at Newcastle
items.summary:
If Mikel Arteta was delighted to see the back of Eddie Howe as Newcastle’s head coach, the bad news is that another similarly awkward technical area adversary has been installed at St James’ Park.
If Arsenal’s manager never seemed to relish trips to face Howe’s old team, Arteta certainly did not enj
items.text:
If Mikel Arteta was delighted to see the back of Eddie Howe as Newcastle’s head coach, the bad news is that another similarly awkward technical area adversary has been installed at St James’ Park.
If Arsenal’s manager never seemed to relish trips to face Howe’s old team, Arteta certainly did not enjoy this latest trip to Tyneside where Matthias Jaissle’s initially overwhelmed team fought back to earn a point courtesy of a stellar second-half performance.
At half-time the crowd had felt close to turning against Jaissle but he held his nerve and, thanks to a triple substitution and smart tactical rejig suggested that he is no mug after all.
It left Arsenal – who lost their goalkeeper David Raya to a potentially significant second-half shoulder injury – still top of the Premier League, six points clear of Brighton and Manchester City and Arteta with a face like thunder.
Only last week Bruno Guimarães claimed he was “beloved” by Newcastle fans but the club’a former captain turned Arsenal midfielder found himself serenaded by a soundtrack of boos of the sort usually reserved for Sunderland players.
Newcastle’s problem is that, despite spending an awful lot of money, they have struggled to replace last season’s now departed star trio – Guimarães, Sandro Tonali and Anthony Gordon.
That reality perhaps left Howe’s successor making a not so subtle point with his team sheet here.
Of Jaissle’s starting XI only the goalkeeper, Lukas Hornicek, the right-back Amar Dedic and the midfielder Sean Steur were signed this summer.
The other five new faces that arrived during a close season that saw a total of around £275m invested on newcomers were either benched (Nico González and Matias Fernandez-Pardo) or did not make the 20-man match day squad (Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Touré). Admittedly Ewen Jaouen is injured but, given that Bamba and Touré cost a combined £78.5m their total omission represented quite a statement. Ditto the decision to leave González and Fernandez-Pardo and their individual £50m plus price tags on the bench.
Back on the pitch the jury remained out on Hornicek. The Czech international has made some excellent saves this season but, here, his kicking proved pretty much uniformly poor and he was fortunate to be reprieved when he hesitated too long as the impressive Kai Harvertz closed in.
Jaissle’s technical frustration with his goalkeeper proved well apparent as Arsenal took increasing control of a first half that saw Newcastle’s lone striker, William Osula isolated and even their normally imperious England left back Lewis-Hall, given a thorough workout by Noni Madueke.
Much to Arteta’s chagrin, Lewis Miley, preferred to González in the midfield holding role, did his very best to slow the tempo but ultimately it proved a forlorn task. The red tide could only be stemmed for so long.
When Havertz dispossessed Hall in the wake of the latter miscontrolling a long ball, he cut inside and slid a highly intelligent, beautifully calibrated, pass across to the on-rushing Eberechi Eze. Without breaking stride, Eze exhibited perfect balance unleashed a gorgeous first-time shot that arrowed, inexorably, passed the powerless Hornicek.
As the home fans fell eerily silent, Arteta and his staff celebrated a goal sufficiently special to rebuke suggestions that his side are all about efficiency at the expense of artistry these days.
Given that on those rare moments when Newcastle’s attack looked as if it might flicker into life, Declan Rice always seemed on hand to reinforce his defence and smother any sort of danger, the omens were not bright for Jaissle.
Indeed it was a struggle to recall his side making a meaningful attacking touch inside Arsenal’s box and fans stationed near the home dugouts made their feelings plain to the manager.
Arsenal’s pressing was so good that Newcastle were left seemingly incapable of playing short passes and, instead found themselves reduced to aimless long balls. With Rice and Martin Ødegaard apparently operating on a different midfield planet an equaliser felt like a distant dream.
Yet however far fetched that vision was something Harvey Barnes would prove fully capable of buying into. The left winger is Newcastle’s best finisher. And when, early in the second half, Ødegaard made an uncharacteristic error, his heavy touch sliced the ball in Osula’s direction.
Once the Dane played it into the path of Barnes in it took a single, steadying, touch and an assured finish to leave the hitherto redundant David Raya picking his shot out of the net.
Jaissle’s introduction of Tino Livramento, Jacob Ramsey and Anthony Elanga - who, incidentally, were all at Newcastle last season - at the expense of Dedic, Steur and Jacob Murphy at the interval was. paying dividends. Suddenly, almost astonishingly, Arsenal were the team in danger of being pressed into submission.
The home side had begun closing their guests down far higher up the pitch and, along the way had morphed into an infinitely more menacing team.
Soon, they were ahead in the wake of a Hall corner headed down by Dan Burn, allowing Malick Thiaw to stab the ball beyond Raya.
Shortly afterwards Arsenal’s goalkeeper was helped off the pitch in evident pain after sustaining a nasty looking left shoulder injury during an ostensibly benign collision with Osula. On came Kepa Arrizabalaga in a triple substitution also featuring the withdrawl of Guimarães.
Madueke though was still around and he reminded everyone of his presence by meeting the counter-attacking Ødegaard’s stellar pass, dummying a couple of defenders and watching his slightly deflected shot evade Hornicek’s grasp.

items.text:
Who was 'a consistent threat'? Newcastle v Arsenal player ratings
- Published
Arsenal and Newcastle played out an entertaining 2-2 draw at St James' Park on Saturday.
The Gunners took the lead through Eberechi Eze in the first half before Harvey Barnes equalised after the break.
The hosts went ahead when Malick Thiaw bundled in from a corner before Noni Madueke brought the Gunners level with an excellent strike, and that is how it finished.
BBC Sport's Alex Howell has rated the players - and you can have your say too.
- What do BBC Sport's player ratings mean? 
  - Published21 August
Newcastle United
Lukas Hornicek: His kicking was slightly erratic. Nearly got caught on the ball by Kai Havertz after taking too long to release it. Could have done better with the second Arsenal goal. 5
Amar Dedic: Booked after pulling back Eberechi Eze and had a tough evening against the England forward. 5
Malick Thiaw: Scored the goal to put Newcastle in front, which capped an excellent performance in central defence. 8
Dan Burn: Some crucial clearances in the first half and played a big part as Newcastle took the lead. 7
Lewis Hall: A big error for the opening goal when he failed to deal with a clipped ball over the top. The left back redeemed himself with a crucial block to deny Noni Madueke and provided some excellent deliveries into the Arsenal box. 7
Sean Steur: Showed quality on the ball and a calmness you do not often see in an 18-year-old, but taken off at half time. 6
Lewis Miley: Quality on the ball and worked well with Steur. Was the deepest of the Newcastle midfield in the second half. 7
Jacob Murphy: An early shot and tried to catch David Raya off his line, but also taken off at the break after a quiet first half. 5
Joe Willock: An all-action performance and his physicality was a big reason why Newcastle improved in the second half. 7
Harvey Barnes: An excellent finish to bring Newcastle level and was always direct. 8
William Osula: Isolated as he led the Newcastle attack but did very well to assist his side's opening goal. 7
Subs:
Tino Livramento (on 46, Dedic): Made a huge impact after coming on at half-time. 7
Anthony Elanga (on 46, Murphy): His pace meant Newcastle always had an option in behind. 6
Jacob Ramsey (on 46, Steur): Added drive to the midfield. 7
Sven Botman (on 92, Hall)
Subs not used: Pope, Schar, Gonzalez, Wissa, Fernandez-Pardo.
Arsenal
David Raya: Was taken off with what looked like a serious shoulder problem after conceding twice. 5
Jurrien Timber: Arsenal used the Dutchman's aerial ability to get up the pitch quickly. Picked up some dangerous positions when the Gunners had the ball. 6
Ezri Konsa: The centre-back looked to be cruising before Arsenal conceded twice in the second half. 6
Gabriel Magalhaes: Got caught up in a battle with Osula as Arsenal conceded a second to go behind. 6
Riccardo Calafiori: A quieter attacking display than usual from the marauding left-back. 6
Declan Rice: Started the game very well but could not stop the Newcastle turnaround. 7
Bruno Guimaraes: Had to deal with a hostile reception whenever he was on the ball. Should have scored in the first half with a great chance and then taken off. 5
Martin Odegaard: An uncharacteristic mistake to gift Newcastle a way back into the match, but then made amends by setting up Madueke. 6
Eberechi Eze: Scored the opening goal of the game with a powerful finish. Looked sharp and provided an outlet. 7
Noni Madueke: Lots of positive moments from the winger and scored a great goal to bring Arsenal level. A consistent threat. 8
Kai Havertz: Plenty of smart play and almost nicked a goal when he closed down Hornicek. Provided a great pass for Eze's goal. 7
Subs:
Kepa Arrizabalaga (on 70, Raya): Made a couple of smart stops. 6
Myles Lewis-Skelly (on 70, Guimaraes): A solid performance from the bench. 7

items.title: 'The world got to see today' - who is new Spurs star Williams-Barnett?
items.summary:
'The world got to see today' - who is new Spurs star Williams-Barnett?
- Published
Luca Williams-Barnett's performance in his first Premier League start was that good it had two of his Tottenham team-mates labelling him "incredible".
The 18-year-old winger delivered the opener with his first senior
items.text:
'The world got to see today' - who is new Spurs star Williams-Barnett?
- Published
Luca Williams-Barnett's performance in his first Premier League start was that good it had two of his Tottenham team-mates labelling him "incredible".
The 18-year-old winger delivered the opener with his first senior goal and then played a pivotal role in Dominic Solanke's second as Spurs comfortably beat Ipswich 2-0 at home.
As full debuts go, it does not get much better than that.
Yet what might be a sign of the excitement about his potential was manager Roberto de Zerbi calmly explaining that "his talent is bigger than this performance".
The Tottenham boss obviously believes this is just the beginning for the talented teenager.
Williams-Barnett became the youngest Spurs player to score in the Premier League since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007.
They would be pretty impressive footsteps to follow in if he was to get close to the player Bale once was for the north London club.
But for the slightest of touches on his fizzed ball across the area from Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton before Solanke turned home, Williams-Barnett would have become the second-youngest player ever to both score and assist in a Premier League game, aged just 18 years and 51 days old.
Only Michael Owen, who did it at 17 years and 364 days for Liverpool in 1997, would have done it at a younger age.
"He's incredible, honestly," Solanke told Final Score. "We get to see him every day in training so we know what a player he is - the confidence he has, the ability he has.
"The world got to see it today, which is great for him. His confidence and ability is amazing. He'll help us a lot."
Born in Luton, built at Tottenham
Williams-Barnett was born in Luton and played for his hometown club before moving to Spurs at the age of 10.
The teenager has been generating excitement with his performances for the club's underage teams for some time.
Back in the 2023-24 season, he played for Tottenham's Under-18s aged just 15 and in the following campaign he scored the Under-18 Premier League goal of the season against Leicester having become renowned for fine long-range strikes.
Williams-Barnett has been around Tottenham's first-team since the 2024-25 campaign as he was on the bench for three Europa League games and a Premier League match but his debut came last season as a substitute in a Carabao Cup game against Doncaster Rovers under previous boss Thomas Frank.
Last December, he scored five goals in a Under-19 UEFA Youth League game against Slavia Prague.
But this season looks to be his real breakthrough.
Williams-Barnett featured in the EFL Cup as a substitute in a 5-1 victory over Charlton in August before coming off the bench against Crystal Palace and Leeds in the Premier League.
'He's just an incredible football player'
Yet it was still a bold choice from De Zerbi to make Williams-Barnett the club's sixth youngest starter in Premier League history given Spurs were coming into this game on the back of a defeat by Leeds United which checked a recent upturn in form.
However, the Spurs boss was rewarded with a man-of-the-match worthy display.
His goal was one of endeavour as he brushed in front of Ipswich defender Abdoul Ouattara to reach Pedro Porro's cross and become the club's youngest scorer on their Premier League full debut.
Throughout the game, he was looking for the ball constantly and not afraid to run with it and try to make things happen.
"Obviously I am so happy for him, every day in the training session he shows his quality," Tottenham defender Destiny Udogie told BBC Match of the Day.
"Honestly he's just an incredible football player. I hope he keeps doing what he's doing."
The winger was unfortunate not to get the assist but the goal does not happen without his powerful cross.
The England youth international was not afraid to take on a shot and his four attempts were all on target while he had a passing accuracy of 77.4% among his 44 touches.
Only Solanke took on more shots in the game with four of his five on target.
"To see him come in and do that on his first Premier League start is crazy," added Solanke.
"He's a great person and is obviously still young, you know what young boys are like.
"But he's very dedicated and so brave on the ball which is great, in his position I think you need that."
Maddison the mentor
Williams-Barnett was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute which brought a standing ovation from the crowd but, with the Brazilian then being forced off later on with an injury, there may be more opportunities in the coming weeks.
Obviously there will be more excitement about the talented teenager now which De Zerbi will have to manage and he has picked midfielder James Maddison as a good mentor for the attacker.
"He's played very well, but his talent is bigger than this performance," the Spurs boss told BBC Match of the Day.
"It was the first game and I am very happy, I am very delighted for his performance, but he is a big, big, big talent.
"The management of the younger talented players is different because you can't take risks to lose their enthusiasm and their positive mentality. But I think Tottenham's dressing room now is a good environment for him.
"I put [James] Maddison to play very close to him to speak the same language but also to help him and put him in the best conditions to play. To play with freedom, to play with his qualities because his qualities are very big.
"He has to work hard but also he has to keep the passion to keep the love of football."

items.title: 'Fragile' and 'miles off it' - Alonso's Chelsea honeymoon is over
items.summary:
'Fragile' and 'miles off it' - Alonso's Chelsea honeymoon is over
- Published
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is already in firefighting mode.
His team were booed by their own supporters at several points during a dominant 4-1 Leeds victory at Stamford Bridge, their first win there since 1999.
The first
items.text:
'Fragile' and 'miles off it' - Alonso's Chelsea honeymoon is over
- Published
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is already in firefighting mode.
His team were booed by their own supporters at several points during a dominant 4-1 Leeds victory at Stamford Bridge, their first win there since 1999.
The first negative reaction came at half-time while the score was still 1-1. The ground then began to empty after the third and fourth Leeds goals, and the fans remaining voiced their dissent once more at the final whistle.
Although there were mitigating circumstances, including a potentially harsh penalty decision against them and the loss of midfielder Moises Caicedo to injury, joining a five-strong list of players on the treatment table, the defeat was thoroughly deserved.
It leaves Chelsea with three losses in their past four Premier League matches and they have slipped from fifth place to eighth, already 14 points behind league leaders Arsenal.
In October, Tottenham won at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the Premier League era, while the 1-0 defeat at bottom club Sunderland before the international break was another alarm bell.
It is the first time since 1967 that Chelsea have lost at home to both Leeds and Spurs in the same season.
"We need to find solutions, for sure, because there will be setbacks during any game," Alonso said after the match.
"To be able to go through that and to know that it's still so long to play, it's something mandatory in this competition and today I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment mentally.
"When we received a punch we didn't recover that strongly."
Indeed, even when Chelsea have been winning matches, they have often looked unconvincing.
Yet Blues supporters chanted their new manager's name and seemed optimistic after the summer transfer business - despite a disappointing 10th-place finish last season.
Club record £117m signing Morgan Rogers was joined by the experienced trio of Emiliano Martinez, Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson.
It was the clinical finishing of Rogers, along with Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro earlier in the season, that masked the underlying fragility of Alonso's team.
Before this weekend, the Blues ranked 14th for expected goal difference and were joint 12th in Opta's expected points table.
After their latest setback, ex-England forward and BBC Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer said: "Chelsea were all over the place. Once Moises Caicedo went off injured early on, there was no physicality and they looked weak.
"They hardly created anything going forward and the back four didn't look comfortable. There was no desire, cohesion or fight from the home side, but we shouldn't take anything away from Leeds.
"Two weeks ago Chelsea were bullied by Sunderland centre-forward Brian Brobbey and they let Dominic Calvert-Lewin do the same today, which is alarming.
"It's fair to say Xabi Alonso's honeymoon period is over. He needs to tell his players this simply isn't good enough. They are miles off it and have to do better in every department."
So what's going wrong?
In Alonso's defence, Chelsea had problems before his arrival.
They finished 10th last season, having been outrun in 37 of their 38 matches, and had three managers during a chaotic campaign.
Remarkably, Chelsea have seven more points from corresponding fixtures this season and last, but it mostly serves to show how low the bar was set.
Champions League qualification was again the club's pre-season target and Alonso's appointment was designed to bring stability and authority.
The former Real Madrid and Liverpool midfielder had an impressive playing career and earned much early admiration as a manager, guiding Bayer Leverkusen to a league and cup double in 2024.
However, the Spaniard, who was sacked by Real Madrid last season, has yet to establish any real consistency - beyond his defence leaking goals regularly.
Only Crystal Palace, Coventry City and Ipswich Town have conceded more goals than Chelsea this season.
Chelsea are also now averaging fewer than a goal per game since Joao Pedro suffered a thigh injury in training. Alongside Pedro and now Caicedo, Jorrel Hato, Maxence Lacroix, Reece James and Jamie Gittens are also injured.
It highlights how they have gained little benefit of having a season without European football.
Alonso is also beginning to face criticism from sections of the fanbase for both his team selections and substitutions.
Chief among the reasons is the constant chopping and changing of the starting XI, having now made 28 line-up changes (behind only Tottenham) while also switching between back-four and back-three systems.
In addition, Alonso is being criticised for his use of personnel, having deployed Pedro Neto as a striker on two occasions and, some would argue, not made enough use of exciting young winger Estevao.
Uncharted territory for Alonso
Against Leeds he gave striker Emmanuel Emegha his first start alongside Estevao and, although the Dutch striker scored, the pair were the first players he substituted while Chelsea were chasing the game at 3-1 down.
Similarly, his late in-game interventions are under scrutiny, including the decision to bring on striker Welbeck only in the 90th minute of the defeat by Spurs.
He took until the 64th minute to make changes against Leeds when Chelsea were already 3-1 down. Only three clubs had made more substitutions in the last 15 minutes than Chelsea in the league this season.
Given Leeds' strengths, Chelsea should have been better prepared for what was coming. Before kick-off, Leeds had applied more high-intensity pressures in the opposition half than any other team in the Premier League.
They had also generated the most expected goals from set-pieces and won the most duels. Leeds maintained those trends at Stamford Bridge against a Chelsea side often accused of being soft.
Chelsea have had problems in recent seasons, but this was still their worst home defeat since a 4-1 loss to Brentford in 2022.

items.summary:

South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus held an online watchalong during the Ireland vs Springboks match in the Nations Championship while serving a suspension from World Rugby; part of Er
items.text:
Rassie Erasmus: South Africa head coach running the risk of breaching suspension after holding online watchalong
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus held an online watchalong during the Ireland vs Springboks match in the Nations Championship while serving a suspension from World Rugby; part of Erasmus' ban covers "direct or indirect contact with team management on matchdays"
Saturday 21 November 2026 19:47, UK
South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus went ahead with an online watchalong during Ireland's victory over his team in the Nations Championship on Saturday.
Erasmus is serving a six-match suspension handed down by World Rugby following extraordinary claims, questioning whether "match-fixing" and "manipulation" was occurring in rugby after his side's defeat to France in Paris last week.
The 54-year-old was suspended for "public criticism of match officials, undermining the integrity of individuals or the sport, and fuelling online abuse".
Erasmus organised a free watchalong for anyone to sign up and view him react to the Test match as he watched it unfold from his Dublin hotel.
After a brief welcome, Erasmus kept himself on mute during both halves of the match, where he could be seen clapping at times, gazing intently at a TV, apparently shouting into what presumably was a phone and thumping his table in frustration when Ireland won 20-17.
But he did come off mute at half-time to outline what he thought would be under discussion in the break. He said: "We've not been playing perfect.
"If we step it up I think we'll be in this match. I think they've been really clinical but I'd have been much more worried if we'd played perfect and we're not currently playing perfect and we shouldn't just play to get one bonus point.
"I think will be the gist of what's happening at half-time."
Erasmus' ban covers the following:
"The suspension applies with immediate effect, applies to international matches, and includes any matchday involvement including coaching, direct or indirect contact with team management or players on matchdays; entering the stadium, coaches' box, playing enclosure, technical area, approaching and/or communicating with match officials on matchday; engaging in any 'feedback' process with match officials; and engaging in media duties during the suspension."
Regarding the "direct or indirect contact with team management or players on matchdays" element of his suspension, Sky Sports sought guidance on the potential for one of South Africa's coaching staff or management set-up signing up, listening to and watching the reactions and comments of their suspended head coach during the contest.
While this specific scenario is not covered by the guidelines, Sky Sports understands Erasmus' plan could be considered a breach by rugby's governing body.
There was, though, a short delay to the broadcast feed Erasmus was using.
South Africa Rugby released a statement requesting a full misconduct hearing in an immediate response to the sanction, but it is understood formal confirmation of an intention to appeal is yet to be received at World Rugby.
Erasmus has now been suspended three times in five years for these sorts of incidents.
During the 2021 British and Irish Lions series in South Africa, after the Springboks lost the first Test, Erasmus broadcast an hour-long critique of Australian referee Nic Berry, and was eventually handed a two-month ban from all rugby activity and a 10-month matchday ban.
In 2022 he received a two-Test ban after sarcastic social media posts following back-to-back South Africa defeats to Ireland and France. A video critical of referee Wayne Barnes led to the official revealing he and his family had received death threats.
On Wednesday, SA Rugby released a statement "condemning the online abuse of officials" following confirmation of Erasmus' ban.

items.summary:
Why can't we get rid of antibiotic resistance?

items.text:
Why can't we get rid of antibiotic resistance?
November 21, 2026
"The threat is immense," said Jean Pierre Nyemazi, acting director of the World Health Organization's department of antimicrobial resistance, during a virtual press conference recently. "An estimated cumulative number of 39 million deaths directly attributable to AMR [antimicrobial resistance] would occur in the next 25 years."
It was, however, the stated goal of World Health Organization, or WHO, member statesto reduce the mortality rate caused by AMR by 10% until 2030, Nyemazi added. "When we see the trend, the investments, the action, we don't think we are on the right track."
Without antibiotics, today's modern medicine would not exist
A world without effective antibiotics would be like traveling back to the days in which even the smallest infection was life-threatening, said Can Imirzalioglu, director of the Institute of Medical Microbiology at Justus Liebig University Giessen. "If antibiotics were no longer effective, modern medicine as we know it today would no longer be possible at all."
Imirzalioglu is not only an expert on antibiotic resistance but also on "One Health," a concept adopted in 2004 by experts in human medicine, veterinary medicine and nature conservation. It recognizes that the health of humans, animals and the environment is closely interconnected.
After all, antibiotics and antimicrobial-resistant germs are not just a problem in hospitals. They can also be found in animal shelters, in animal products, in waste water, in fertilizers and in plants. "One Health tries to keep an eye on all of this," Imirzalioglu said.
For hospitals and doctors' offices this means that antibiotics must be used as selectively and purposefully as possible. To this end, research is focused primarily on developing better and faster diagnostic methods.
In Germany, antibiotics were frequently prescribed against respiratory or urinary tract infections, Imirzalioglu said. But antibiotics are only effective against bacteria. If a virus causes the infection, they are ineffective.
Nonetheless, every antibiotics dose has consequences: it damages our gut microbiome. This consists of billions of micro-organisms, primarily bacteria, which are essential for digestion, metabolism and the immune system. "If we damage the [bacteria], resistant pathogens can spread and take their place," Imirzalioglu said.
Another problem was that such a spreading of resistant pathogens in the gut often went unnoticed and without causing symptoms, he added.
So people became "carriers of resistant pathogens, which they, in turn, release back into their environment."
In this way, resistant pathogens make their way out of hospitals via toilets and sinks into wastewater and, from there, into the Baltic Sea, where they are ingested by wild birds. This pathway was traced in a study by Katharina Schaufler, a veterinarian and microbiologist at the Helmholtz Institute for One Health (HIOH).
Why factory farming exacerbates the problem
Antibiotics have not only been used in humans on a large scale over a long time, excessive use in veterinary medicine has also led to resistance to nearly all available antibiotics, Schaufler said.
In 2006, an EU-wide ban on the use of antibiotics as growth promoters in animal feedcame into effect. Since then, antibiotics may only be applied as part of veterinary treatment.
The problem is that due to factory farming the use of antibiotics for medical purposes is a permanent necessity. The mere fact that animals live together in confined spaces causes infections to spread rapidly.
Lack of space as well as boredom lead the animals to injure each other and this happens in an environment where, in Schaufler's words, "there's already a high level of bacterial pressure."
Through fertilizers, antibiotic-resistant pathogens enter the environment. "It has been proven that, for example, resistant bacteria can still be found on lettuce heads," the veterinarian said. Resistant bacteria were also found time and again on meat.
National solutions are also falling short. In many countries, antibiotics are still a standard additive in animal feed, Schaufler said. And in such countries, antibiotics could be obtained in drugstores without prescriptions, Imirzalioglu added. Both say that all of this makes the global fight against antibiotic resistance more difficult.
Combating antibiotic resistance means preventing infections
Political will is of the essence when it comes to combating antibiotic resistance. Imirzalioglu works at Guardian, a project funded by the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space.
The aim of the project is to prevent outbreaks of diseases caused by resistant bacteria by monitoring and analyzing wastewater in the German state of Hesse.
At EU level, Imirzalioglu is also an advisor at the Antimicrobial Resistance One Health Network. He sums up his experience with policymakers: "The experts and working groups have great ideas, and then these are often scaled back or stifled during the initial stages."
Perhaps the lack of political will so far is one of the reasons why the WHO's Nyemazi is issuing an appeal to every individual: Preventing antibiotic resistance means preventing infections, through hygiene, regular vaccinations and doctor's appointments as well as taking medications in accordance with prescriptions.
This article was originally published in German.

items.title: 'Officials can't use common sense' - was Rogers handball correct?
items.summary:
'Officials can't use common sense' - was Rogers handball correct?
- Published
It is rare when a key handball decision is given for the widespread response to be "that is correct".
Often the discussion centres on the desire for a seemingly more lenient interpretation taking into account perceived int
items.text:
'Officials can't use common sense' - was Rogers handball correct?
- Published
It is rare when a key handball decision is given for the widespread response to be "that is correct".
Often the discussion centres on the desire for a seemingly more lenient interpretation taking into account perceived intent.
And that is again a talking point after the crucial penalty given against Chelsea in Saturday's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds which ended up putting the visitors ahead for the first time.
Interestingly, despite the perception, handball penalties are much rarer in the Premier League compared with the other top five leagues in Europe.
Last season, there were 22 penalties for handball in the English top flight's 380 games - easily the lowest tally.
Spain's La Liga (36) and Italy's Serie A (38) produced the most.
This season in the Premier League there have been three in 106 matches - less than in 2025-26.
So why was the penalty given against Chelsea's Morgan Rogers?
Why the penalty was given
The feeling among Premier League clubs is that handball is in a good place now, where the arm must either be fully extended away from the body, raised, or be a deliberate act to be punishable.
And it is the last of these that applied to the penalty given against Rogers, which to some might seem a bit harsh, considering the Premier League's more relaxed interpretation of handball.
There are, however, a few key reasons why referee Michael Oliver pointed to the spot, why the video assistant referee (VAR) did not intervene, and why it will be judged as a correct decision.
Two of the factors which a referee looks for when judging a potential handball apply here.
First, how far the ball travelled.
As Jayden Bogle's shot was from distance, a defender is considered to have more time to adjust their body and react - and thus avoid a potential handball.
Most important in this case is the movement of the arm.
When Bogle shoots, Rogers' arm is not raised - but it comes up to the flight of the ball.
Crucially, had Rogers kept his arm in its original position - lower and level with his midriff - there would not have been a handball offence.
What does this mean? Put simply, if the ball would have hit the body if it had not come off the arm, it is considered to have no impact.
But this case was different. Rogers raised his arm and that is what led to the ball being deflected away. This is considered a deliberate act, and this trumps all other considerations.
Was there any case not to give it?
Perhaps there was a question about whether the ball hit Rogers too high on his arm, and thus should not be a handball offence.
It was close, but it looked like it was in what the laws call the 'red zone', the part of the arm which is punishable for handball.
But this really would be the only reason the VAR, Michael Salisbury, would have any cause to consider an on-field review.
We saw a similar case last season, in terms of how this kind of handball offence is judged - coincidentally involving a penalty awarded to Leeds.
As Anton Stach's powerful strike arrowed towards goal, Everton defender James Tarkowski leaned to his left in an attempt to block the shot - and did so with his arm, which was tucked tightly to the side of his body.
Everton manager David Moyes described the decision as "wrong", but it was absolutely correct in law.
That Tarkowski's arm was close to his side was irrelevant because of the deliberate act of leaning into the path of the ball.
Likewise, Rogers raised his arm to stop the ball and a penalty was a justifiable call.
Decision underlines dissatisfaction with handball law
Despite the Premier League having a more lenient interpretation of the handball law already, it is clear that many observers would like it to go further.
For example, BBC Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer echoed many when he said there should be more intent for a handball.
"I didn't agree with the penalty when Michael Oliver gave it," he said.
"I know once the on-field decision is made there is a high bar to review it, but I don't think officials are allowed to use common sense.
"Morgan Rogers is not deliberately trying to stop the ball. He just doesn't want it hitting him in the face.
"Although the penalty came at an important point in the match, Chelsea were deservedly beaten by a much stronger, far more physical and better-organised Leeds team."
Rogers may argue he raised his arm to protect his face.
This is one of the possible mitigating factors, but usually only applies when a player raises their hands to their face - not using the arm as a barrier.
Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso said that, while he did not "want to make a big thing about it", the penalty should not have been awarded.
"For me it was quite a harsh decision," he told Sky Sports. "I would not have given a penalty. I don't want to make a big thing about it but for me it's not a penalty."

A gun battle between Mexican soldiers and alleged gang members in the city of Guasave, in the state of Sinaloa, ended with special forces detaining senior members of the Beltran Leyva drug trafficking network, Mexican offici
items.text:
Mexican special forces arrest drug kingpin 'Chapo Isidro'
November 21, 2026
A gun battle between Mexican soldiers and alleged gang members in the city of Guasave, in the state of Sinaloa, ended with special forces detaining senior members of the Beltran Leyva drug trafficking network, Mexican officials said on Saturday.
The gang is aligned with one of the factions of the powerful Sinaloa cartel.
Authorities said the overnight raid resulted in capture of the suspected drug kingpin Fausto Isidro Meza F., better known as "Chapo Isidro," who is believed to be the leader of Beltran Leyva.
FBI offering millions for 'Chapo Isidro'
The 44-year-old Mexican national is one of the FBI's ten most wanted fugitives. The US law enforcement agency claims his group is responsible for smuggling "large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl, and marijuana into the United States," and has offered a $5 million (€4.56 million) reward for information leading to his arrest.
He is also wanted in Mexico on charges including organized crime.
On Saturday, Mexican authorities said the raid was conducted due to "intelligence coordination" between Mexico's military and US agencies.
The three detainees were transported to Mexico City "to be placed at the disposal of the competent prosecutorial authorities," the military said.
It was not immediately clear if "Chapo Isidro" will be extradited to the US.
Roads blocked in Sinaloa
The troops used "stealth and surprise" to reach the area, establishing a perimeter around the drug dealer's location and then moving in from multiple directions, according Mexico's US embassy.
Unverified videos from Guasave, however, showed military helicopters firing at ground targets and sports fans scrambling for safety during a baseball game. Some of the violence in the western Mexican city seems to have taken place after Chapo Isidro was arrested, with drug cartels attempting to retaliate against the authorities and civilians for the move.
Mexico's defense ministry confirmed cartel members set up roadblocks in the area, but added that security forces were assisting local authorities in restoring order.
The Guasave raid is only the latest in a string of high-profile moves against senior leaders of Mexico's illegal drug trade. Less than two weeks ago, Mexican navy announced the arrest of Rafael A., suspected of leading a cartel cell active in the states of Jalisco and Michoacan.
President Claudia Sheinbaum is facing pressure from Donald Trump, who has threatened to take military action against cartels on Mexican territory.

items.title: Storms expected on both coasts threatens Thanksgiving travel
items.summary:
Storms expected on both coasts threatens Thanksgiving travel
Before worrying about the temperature of the turkey, travelers could face a different type of uncertainty next week. This time, it's the weather — and it's affecting both U.S. coasts.
"I know there's a lot of travel for many of you as you
items.text:
Storms expected on both coasts threatens Thanksgiving travel
Before worrying about the temperature of the turkey, travelers could face a different type of uncertainty next week. This time, it's the weather — and it's affecting both U.S. coasts.
"I know there's a lot of travel for many of you as you head into the Thanksgiving holiday, but I'm going to ask you all to consider not traveling unless it is absolutely essential," said San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie on X Friday. He said the city is preparing this weekend for extreme high tides and rain that could hit the area Monday afternoon through Wednesday.
Over the past week, cities in California saw mudslides, waterspouts and flooding while Florida also saw coastal flooding and inundated streets. A new set of storms are expected to hit both sides of the country early next week, just as travelers head into the holiday week.
It's already been a wet fall in large swaths of the country, thanks in part to a Super El Niño, a natural climate pattern that shifts weather around the world. Devastating flooding in the Southwest U.S. left multiple people dead and hundreds stranded, and California and the Pacific Northwest have seen high sea level and multiple strong atmospheric rivers.
Atmospheric rivers are here to stay
"Take this weekend: get yourself ready," Lurie, the San Francisco mayor, said after a call with the National Weather Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.
Rain and snow, in higher elevations, is possible over parts of the northwest and northern California on Saturday, according to the NWS.
The West Coast is forecasted to see an atmospheric river, a narrow band of water vapor pushed by the wind, on Monday. Another is expected for the Pacific Northwest later in the week, according to the Center for Western Weather and Water Extremes. Atmospheric rivers hang over an area and dump precipitation. They can cause months worth of rain in just a few days.
The center expects two to four inches of precipitation over northern California and southern Oregon through Wednesday.
Coastal flood advisories are also in effect through Monday morning in the Bay Area, the NWS said. This comes on top of historic high tides, known as King tides.
Travel troubles could persist after Thanksgiving
A storm that started in Florida Friday will move north to the Mid-Atlantic and into the Northeast by Sunday evening, according to the NWS.
Some of the heaviest rain could be seen on the coast of the Carolinas through Sunday morning. Then, heavy rain is expected to move up the coast, said Dan Hoffman, a meteorologist at the National Weather Service in Baltimore, Md.
Hoffman said during a busy travel week, even with the weather not expected to bring flooding or strong winds, it "doesn't usually take too much to cause things to start to have delays."
As for New England, Andrew Loconto, a meteorologist at the NWS in Norton, Mass., said the storm this weekend is not forecasted to be as big as another storm hitting the region after Thanksgiving. "That could be more impacts for people coming back home," Loconto said, pointing to another highly anticipated day across the U.S. — Black Friday.

Russia-bound ship attacked in Gulf of Finland

A Russian cargo vessel bound for the country's Baltic Kaliningrad territory has been hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, Russian and Finnish authorities say.
The ship - the Sparta II - caught on fire after the strike on Satu
items.text:
Russia-bound ship attacked in Gulf of Finland
- Published
A Russian cargo vessel bound for the country's Baltic Kaliningrad territory has been hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, Russian and Finnish authorities say.
The ship - the Sparta II - caught on fire after the strike on Saturday, and drifted into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack.
"War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said, adding: "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor."
Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones were used, according to preliminary information, and that there is "no threat" to their supplies.
The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian company, according to the Ukrainian and American governments.
The company says on its website that it was established within the structure of Russia's defence ministry in 2011, and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex.
On Saturday morning, Finnish defence forces detected the drone attack on the cargo vessel west of Suursaari in the Gulf of Finland, which prompted "temporary aviation and maritime restrictions" over the area.
Shortly after the incident, Finland's defence ministry said a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating the country's airspace, potentially linked to "rescue or tracking operations".
A Russian rescue vessel approached the ship, and was told by the crew that they did not need to be evacuated, Kaliningrad's governor wrote on Telegram, adding: "The crew is currently carrying out the necessary work and plans to continue on its way."
The Finnish Border Guard also said the crew had not been forced to abandon the ship, no environmental damage had been detected, and there was no danger to maritime traffic or people.
Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave that sits between Poland and Lithuania.
Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen said that the Finnish Border Guard are responsible for the investigation into the attack, and are cooperating with other relevant authorities.
Nato has also been informed, the defence ministry said.
The Baltic Sea has become a flashpoint in the Russia-Ukraine war, triggered when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Ukraine has recently ramped up its long-range attacks against Russia beyond the front lines.
Earlier this month, a Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland.

The FBI’s national criminal database has suffered a suspected breach, according to multiple US media reports.
President Donald Trump, who
items.text:
FBI national crime database suffers suspected breach: Reports
The reported hacking is the latest in a string of breaches and outages affecting the US government.
The FBI’s national criminal database has suffered a suspected breach, according to multiple US media reports.
President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly downplayed breaches affecting departments within his administration, appeared to confirm the FBI hacking during a television interview on Saturday.
“Well, we just heard about it, and I will say that it’s not good. I don’t like that,” Trump told Fox News.
On Friday, CNN and NBC reported that the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which is used by law enforcement agencies across the United States to share information on criminal warrants and background checks, was compromised, citing two people who had been briefed on the matter.
The reported hacking, which would be the second to hit the bureau this year, is the latest in a string of US government breaches and outages that have alarmed officials over the past week.
In a separate incident, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture.
The FBI and USDA did not immediately return Al Jazeera’s request for comment.
In the interview on Saturday, Trump suggested the hack of the FBI’s crucial database could be viewed with “a positive spin”.
“Maybe we’ll learn things that we would have never learned otherwise. You had the Russia, Russia, Russia hoax. You had all these other hoaxes,” he said in an apparent reference to his discontent with the FBI’s investigation into Russian interference in the 2016 US election.
In September, the FBI said it was investigating an apparent breach by a cyber group that claimed it had stolen sensitive information on the bureau’s 38,000 employees.
Additionally, in March, the agency said it had been investigating “suspicious activities” on some of its internal systems, The Associated Press news agency reported.
FBI Director Kash Patel, who has not publicly commented on the most recent hacking, was not present for a Wednesday hearing at the US Capitol to examine threats against the US. Patel’s deputy, Christopher Raia, attended in his place, joining US Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton.

items.title: Noah Okafor stars as Leeds hammer Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge
items.summary:
Chelsea v Leeds
Noah Okafor stars as Leeds hammer Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge
Noah Okafor scored twice as Leeds beat Chelsea 4-1 to record their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years.
Daniel Farke's team conceded six here earlier this season. That wild defeat in the Carabao Cup
items.text:
Chelsea v Leeds
Noah Okafor stars as Leeds hammer Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge
Noah Okafor scored twice as Leeds beat Chelsea 4-1 to record their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years.
Daniel Farke's team conceded six here earlier this season. That wild defeat in the Carabao Cup in September came at a time when Chelsea were playing cavalier football that made a 6-3 scoreline seem normal, but they stand now on the brink watching their season fall apart.
This was not what their supporters were sold when Xabi Alonso was appointed amidst broad smiles six months ago.
The leadership spoke then of lessons having been learned and of a corner turned. What must co-owner Behdad Eghbali and his four-strong team of sporting directors have made of Leeds running rings around their team on their own pitch, cantering to an easy victory with minimal resistance?
They began well here, 23-year-old striker Emmanuel Emegha firing them ahead early on his full debut, but within minutes they had gifted Okafor an equaliser, a lovely finish into the corner facilitated by static Chelsea defending.
Morgan Rogers might have been unfortunate to concede the penalty at the start of the second half, which was converted by the excellent Dominic Calvert-Lewin, but that decision was not the reason Chelsea were beaten so soundly.
Okafor quickly made it three for Leeds, Branden Aronson got a fourth in stoppage time, as Chelsea slumped into mid-table.
Leeds were quickly on the front foot and might have lead early. A wonderful cross from James Justin was met by Calvert-Lewin, ghosting between two defenders to head against the crossbar.
Moisés Caicedo was forced off after 20 minutes after a landing awkwardly, arguably the point at which the hosts began to lose their way. Calvert-Lewin soon found room again amongst Chelsea's defence for a header that was this time straight at Emiliano Martínez.
Emegha's goal was Chelsea's only bright spot. Justin made a mess of a clearing header and gave it to Rogers, who nipped past Nico Elvedi and slipped it left for Emegha to take a touch and finish like a striker that had been crashing them in at the Shed End for years.
The manner in which Chelsea let Leeds back level two minutes later will have infuriated Alonso. Josh Acheampong misjudged the bounce of the ball in midfield and Calvert-Lewin stole in and fed Okafor.
There were then three defenders in blue standing motionless around Okafor inside the box as he took aim and rolled the ball into the corner of Martinez's goal.
A wonderful Calvert-Lewin back-flick was inches from putting Leeds ahead. A goal then would have not unfairly reflected the balance of the first half. Chelsea were a mess and were booed off at the break.
It took an age for VAR to determine that Michael Oliver had been correct to call handball against Rogers from Jayden Bogle's driven effort in the 48th minute. Rogers had motioned towards the ball which cannoned away of a combination of upper arm and shoulder, but Chelsea felt aggrieved. From the spot, Calvert-Lewin sent Martinez the wrong way.
Okafor whacked in his second and Leeds' third just before the half-hour, a deflected cross sitting up for a lovely half-volley into the top corner.
Now was the time for another two-goal Chelsea fightback as on that bizarre night in September. Predictably, it never materialised, only another goal from Aronson and more boos for Alonso's players at the end.

items.summary:
Enzo Maresca said Manchester City were denied a "clear" goal in their 1-1 draw with Fulham after Erling Haaland was judged to have fouled goalkeeper Bernd Leno.
Haaland thought he had scored when he bundled the ball over the line from Iliman Ndiaye's cross. But referee Tom Bramall decided Leno had c
items.text:
Enzo Maresca said Manchester City were denied a "clear" goal in their 1-1 draw with Fulham after Erling Haaland was judged to have fouled goalkeeper Bernd Leno.
Haaland thought he had scored when he bundled the ball over the line from Iliman Ndiaye's cross. But referee Tom Bramall decided Leno had control of the ball, a view backed up by VAR.
"I review the goal after the game and from my point of view it is quite clear that it is not a foul, but I am not the guy who decides," Maresca said.
The City boss also said Haaland was convinced he had scored when the ball appeared to slip out of Leno's grasp.
"He was absolutely sure even when they were reviewing the VAR that it was a goal because I asked from the touchline, but the referee decided differently," Maresca said.
City have now gone four Premier League games without a win and nine games in all competitions without a clean sheet.
Fulham, meanwhile, snapped a 20-match losing run against City stretching back to 2011.
- Man City, Enzo Maresca at a crossroads after Premier League stumble
- Fulham finally end 15-year losing run against Man City

"Obviously we knew we lost the last 20 times we played Manchester City, but I told them we would have the chance to beat them if we play with courage, with character," Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa said.
"I won the last time I was here [with Real Madrid], so I thought maybe we would have the chance to win. I think we performed really well. We could win the game."

items.title: FIFPRO slams Bayern's treatment of Musiala: Club has 'duty of care'
items.summary:
Global players' union FIFPRO has criticized Bayern Munich and urged the Bundesliga champions to respect its "duty of care" to Jamal Musiala after senior figures at the club raised the prospect of offloading the player due to his ongoing issues with a neurological dysfunction.
Musiala, 23, made his f
items.text:
Global players' union FIFPRO has criticized Bayern Munich and urged the Bundesliga champions to respect its "duty of care" to Jamal Musiala after senior figures at the club raised the prospect of offloading the player due to his ongoing issues with a neurological dysfunction.
Musiala, 23, made his first senior appearance for Bayern since Sept. 18 with a 20-minute substitute outing in Friday's 1-1 draw against FC Koln -- a game which saw Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane suffer a serious ankle ligament injury which has required surgery.
The Germany forward made a public statement about a "fainting condition" earlier this season after collapsing on the pitch during Bayern's preseason friendlies against Heidenheim and RB Leipzig.
"I have been diagnosed with brief, temporary -- but treatable -- absence seizures resulting from a neurological dysfunction," Musiala said in August.
"[These episodes] are currently simply part of my everyday life. I am receiving the best possible medical care in this regard, and I am very optimistic... There is no additional health risk beyond this."
Despite Musiala's attempts to play down the severity of the condition, however, Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen and senior figure Uli Hoeness have questioned his ability to overcome the problem and questioned the financial cost of his long-term contract.
And board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge echoed those comments Friday by saying Bayern must consider the "financial implications" of Musiala's health issue.
"He [Musiala] has a health-related issue," Rummenigge said.
"It's also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money. As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. I think that's responsible and perfectly normal.
"What we know unfortunately suggests it will be difficult for him to get back to the level he has often shown here in this stadium. I think we've handled the player's situation very carefully, and we all want him to return, ideally in the best possible shape.
"But what happens if that doesn't work out? Then, of course, we'll also have to continue taking the financial implications into account."
With Musiala still battling to regain full health -- the player's recent absence was due to a muscle injury -- FIFPRO has thrown its support behind the forward by condemning Bayern's "coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala."
In statement issued Saturday, FIFPRO said: "FIFPRO is deeply concerned by the repeated public statements from FC Bayern Munich's leadership calling into question the contract of Jamal Musiala as he returns from injury.
"Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession. In FIFPRO's view, this is a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.
- Musiala will 'fight his way back' from injury - Bayern boss Kompany
- Michael Olise to rejoin Bayern Munich for UCL clash vs. Atlético Madrid
- Bayern Munich: Change in treatment caused Musiala collapses
"Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala. Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.
"Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.
"Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.
"Clubs, leagues and player unions have agreed at FIFA level that contractual stability is a core principle of the game. It protects clubs as much as it protects players.
"FIFPRO stands with Jamal Musiala and with all players who honour their commitments. We expect their employers to do the same."
Musiala signed a new contract committing him to Bayern in February 2025 with the player's £21 million ($27m) annual salary second only to Kane at the Allianz Arena.

items.title: Late Thomason strike powers Wrexham to much-needed away win

Lincoln City v Wrexham
Late Thomason strike powers Wrexham to much-needed away win
George Thomason grabbed a late winner as Wrexham secured a welcome 1-0 victory away at Lincoln.
It was a game lacking real quality in the final third at Sincil Bank, but Thomason kept his cool when the moment arose to
items.text:
Lincoln City v Wrexham
Late Thomason strike powers Wrexham to much-needed away win
George Thomason grabbed a late winner as Wrexham secured a welcome 1-0 victory away at Lincoln.
It was a game lacking real quality in the final third at Sincil Bank, but Thomason kept his cool when the moment arose to fire Wrexham to victory with his 82nd-minute strike.
It was a first away league victory for Phil Parkinson's side since the start of September when they beat Millwall 2-0.
The Red Dragons have now gone three games without defeat and will be hoping to use their recent upturn in form as a catalyst towards their playoff push.
For Lincoln, it was the latest bump in the road as the reality of being minnows in the Championship is really beginning to hit home.
Any hopes the international break would bring about a change in fortunes were dashed with a fourth loss on the spin, whilst it is their seventh defeat in nine.
Their only victory in that time was the 4-1 hammering of relegation rivals Burnley, which led to Nicky Hayen's sacking.
The first real chance of the contest fell to the visitors as Callum Doyle nodded wide of the mark from Thomason's delivery into the box.
Down the other end, Rob Street saw his own header well kept out by stopper Anthony Patterson. Defender Demi Elerewe produced a great double block when he prevented Ollie Rathbone from breaking the deadlock.
Patterson was then called into action once more to deny Adam Reach's effort on the half hour mark after good link up play between Reach and Dan Oyegoke.
Street came close to changing the complexion of the respective half-time team talks when he agonisingly fired wide on the stroke of the break.
The second half was a poorer showing than the first with meaningful chances at a premium after the restart.
George Wickens got down low to keep out Rathbone's tame strike from outside the box in a routine bit of keeping.
Patterson barely had to move to stop Andrei Coubis' effort down the middle of his goal.
Dom Jefferies' free-kick did not threaten the visitors, whilst Oyegoke was kept out by another routine Patterson stop heading into the final quarter of an hour.
But the door was eventually unlocked when Thomason snatched the winner with eight minutes to go.
The 25-year-old pounced on a poor back pass and easily slotted home a left-footed effort beyond the on-rushing Wickens for his second goal of the campaign and most importantly to secure the points for the Welsh outfit.
Lincoln chucked on reinforcements to try and salvage something from the game.
Bailey Cadamarteri was denied Wrexham's second, with Patterson keeping out Jefferies right at the end.

items.title: Ballon d'Or winner Kane out a 'few months' after ankle injury in Bayern draw
items.summary:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is set to be sidelined for several months after suffering a ligament tear in his left ankle in the first half of Bayern Munich's draw at home to FC Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday.
Kane was hurt while attempting to get on the end of a deflected Michael Olise cross i
items.text:
Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane is set to be sidelined for several months after suffering a ligament tear in his left ankle in the first half of Bayern Munich's draw at home to FC Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday.
Kane was hurt while attempting to get on the end of a deflected Michael Olise cross in front of goal when Cologne defender Joel Schmied got to the ball first and clattered into Kane's left leg in his follow-through.
Bayern subsequently confirmed that Kane had been diagnosed with a ligament tear following an examination, adding that the England international would be out "for the next few months."
Bayern sporting director Max Eberl said they expect Kane to miss about three months.
Kane, 33, immediately clutched his lower leg after the injury and writhed in pain for a few moments before gingerly getting back to his feet, but he was a virtual bystander for the next couple of minutes.
He gestured to the sideline, sunk to the turf and then received treatment on his ankle before making way for Tom Bischof in the 20th minute, limping off the field alongside two physios.
Kane last month was announced as the men's Ballon d'Or winner after a prolific year with Bayern and England. He is Bayern's first winner of the prestigious award in 45 years and the first English winner in 25 years.
His injury means he is almost certain to miss Bayern's remaining four games in the league phase of the Champions League and could be in jeopardy for the start of the knockout phase in February if Bayern progress.
England will hope that Kane has returned in time for their UEFA Nations League quarterfinal with Norway at the end of March.
Cologne were leading 1-0 at the time of Kane's injury through a 12th-minute goal from Mikey Moore before Nathaniel Brown equalized in the 37th minute.
However, Olise added to Bayern's injury woes as he was substituted at the start of the second half, having hobbled off just before the break following a collision with Tom Krauss.
Olise later left the stadium on crutches, though coach Vincent Kompany said that was a precautionary measure. Bayern later said Olise had a bruised forefoot and would receive treatment in the coming days.
Any prolonged absence for Kane and Olise would be a major blow to Bayern. The pair account for 22 of Bayern's 54 goals (41%) this season and will exacerbate an ongoing personnel shortage for the Bundesliga champions.
Luis Díaz (hamstring), Ismael Saibari (ankle), Serge Gnabry (thigh) and Alphonso Davies (hamstring) are already out for Bayern.
"These are world-class players, you can't replace them, but we have the mentality and we have to bring that now," Kompany said.
"We need incredible performances from players who may not yet be used to this pressure at FC Bayern. We will all try together to turn this situation into a strength. FC Bayern does this time and time again, and that's what we want to do now too."
Despite dominating possession against Cologne, Bayern had only one shot on goal over the 90 minutes as they failed to find a winner. It was the first time Bayern Munich had just one shot on target in a Bundesliga home game since at least 2004-05.
The game was Bayern's first since the November international break, in which Kane scored in England's Nations League wins over Spain and Croatia and gained the men's team record in appearances.
Bayern, who had Kompany back on the sidelines and with his left arm in a sling after illness, are now one point clear of Borussia Dortmund at the top of the Bundesliga ahead of Dortmund's visit to Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday.
"I just wanted to support the team straight away. The only focus was on the game," Kompany said. "Of course, the first time going back up the steps, the first I'm being back on the sideline, it gives you that feeling back, but pretty quickly you go back into trying to do the job."
Information from ESPN Global Research and PA contributed to this report.

items.title: Sources: Tom Brady buys stake in Chelsea after Birmingham exit
items.summary:
Seven-time Super Bowl champion quarterback Tom Brady has purchased a stake in Chelsea soccer club, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network.
The deal would make the NFL legend a minority investor in the Clearlake Capital vehicle that controls Chelsea, sources close to global investment firm added t
items.text:
Seven-time Super Bowl champion quarterback Tom Brady has purchased a stake in Chelsea soccer club, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network.
The deal would make the NFL legend a minority investor in the Clearlake Capital vehicle that controls Chelsea, sources close to global investment firm added to ESPN. Brady is expected to serve as an operating adviser to Clearlake but would not have voting rights with the club.
Brady left the ownership group of second-tier English club Birmingham City earlier this month after becoming a minority owner with a 3.3% stake.
Defense attorney Alex Spiro is part of Brady's ownership group and helped negotiate the deal.
Brady had also held a position on the club's advisory board via a partnership with Birmingham's owner, Knighthead Capital Management, headed by his friend and business partner Tom Wagner.
Todd Boehly and fellow co-owner Mark Walter sold their stakes in Chelsea this past September in a deal that gives Clearlake Capital full control of the English Premier League club.
Private equity firm Clearlake, led by Behdad Eghbali and Jose E. Feliciano, previously owned a 61.5% stake in Chelsea, while U.S. businessmen Walter and Boehly each owned 12.83%. Swiss philanthropist Hansjörg Wyss, who also owned a 12.83% stake, remains a partner in the ownership group.
The consortium bought Chelsea for £2.5 billion ($3.3 billion) in 2022 with a further £1.75 billion ($2.3 billion) committed to investment in the club after former owner Roman Abramovich was sanctioned because of alleged ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin following the country's invasion of Ukraine.
The Financial Times reported that Walter and Boehly will receive £950 million ($1.3 billion) for their combined stake in a deal that values the club at £5 billion ($6.7 billion) including debt.
Neither Chelsea nor Clearlake Capital has replied to ESPN's request for comment about Brady's purchase of shares.
Brady purchased a 5% minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders in 2024 after NFL owners unanimously approved the deal.
ESPN's Adam Schefter and James Olley as well as NFL Network's Ian Rapoport contributed to this report.
